male_mass_kg.text: Toronto Zoo: average male in Canada ~545 kg, Alaskan moose can exceed 680 kg. Commonly cited bull range 380-700 kg (Wikipedia, cross-check only).
male_mass_kg.source_name: Toronto Zoo – American Moose

mass_cross_check.source_name: BC Ministry of Environment moose brochure (archived): adult bulls 450-500 kg

max_mass_kg.text: ADF&G: Alaska-Yukon bulls 1,200-1,600 lb (542-725 kg); 725 kg is the top of the agency range, not a single weighed record. Claims of >770 kg bulls (E Siberia/Alaska) appear only on Wikipedia, unverified.
max_mass_kg.source_name: Alaska Dept. of Fish and Game – Wildlife Notebook: Moose

wild_population.source_name: Alces journal – Population status of moose in North America and Europe circa 2025 (N. America 910,494–1,423,044; Eurasia excl. China/Mongolia/Kazakhstan 1.70–1.95 million)

stronghold.evidence: Alces 2025 survey: Russian Federation ~1.3 million, more than Canada (est. 0.5–1 million) or Sweden (~300–400k)

species.fun_fact: Moose are the largest living deer, and only bulls grow antlers, shed every year.
species.notes: Bull weight varies strongly by region (>10%): BC 450-500 kg, Canada avg ~545 kg, Alaska 542-725 kg, Europe 300-600 kg; Massachusetts gives 270-455+ kg. IUCN treats one species (8 subspecies); some authorities split North American Alces americanus. IUCN species ID 56003281 (assessment last updated 2015). Russian numbers come from winter track counts. WebFetch was blocked in this session; all data from search-result pages.

male_mass_kg.text: WorldAtlas: a typical bull weighs 700-800 lb (320-360 kg); large individuals top 1,000 lb (450 kg).
male_mass_kg.source_name: WorldAtlas – Elk (Cervus canadensis)

mass_cross_check.source_name: Manitoban elk sample (8 adult males, 287.5–477.6 kg, mean ~352 kg) – Wikipedia, cross-check only

max_mass_kg.text: Britannica: exceptional bulls exceed 500 kg; Roosevelt elk (heaviest subspecies) bulls cited to ~590 kg on low-quality sites only. No individual weighed record found.

stronghold.evidence: US totals reported ~1–1.2 million (non-authoritative sites); British Columbia only 35,000–71,500 (2022). Asian wapiti (China, Russia, Mongolia) far fewer. Candidates: US > Canada > Russia/China.

species.fun_fact: Elk were long lumped with Europe's red deer; genetics now split them.
species.notes: IUCN status LC per secondary sources (Mammal Diversity DB, zoo sites); IUCN species page for C. canadensis not seen, so year/trend null. IUCN Tarim red deer assessment notes canadensis elevated to species level for the 2016 Red List assessment. Mass sources conflict (>10%): WorldAtlas 320-360 kg typical vs other sites 320-500 kg; southern California tule elk bulls far smaller. No authoritative continental population figure found (only content-farm ~1 million US).

male_mass_kg.text: Plazi treatment (Handbook of the Mammals of the World text): weight of males 180-270 kg (up to 350 kg).
male_mass_kg.source_name: Plazi – Rusa unicolor (Kerr, 1792) treatment

mass_cross_check.source_name: Journal of Threatened Taxa (Rajasthan sambar): males 225–320 kg, females <180 kg

max_mass_kg.text: Plazi/HMW: 'up to 350 kg'; claims of 550 kg on popular sites are unsupported.

stronghold.evidence: Occurs in 208 protected areas in India; abundant in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala; India populations more stable inside PA network

species.fun_fact: Sambar numbers fell an estimated 30–50% over three generations, mainly from hunting.
species.notes: IUCN VU (first listed 2008; Timmins et al. 2015 assessment) per JoTT and Malaysian BIS citing IUCN; IUCN page itself not seen. Male mass sources differ (>10%): HMW 180-270 kg vs JoTT Rajasthan 225-320 kg; typical male likely <250 kg. No reliable global or Indian population count found (popular '>50,000' unsourced). Female mass: JoTT says <180 kg (no value).

male_mass_kg.text: Polar Bears International FAQ: adult males weigh 350 to more than 600 kg (775 to more than 1,300 lb).
male_mass_kg.source_name: Polar Bears International – FAQ

mass_cross_check.source_name: WWF – Polar Bear: males 800–1,300 lb (363–590 kg)

max_mass_kg.text: PBI: researchers in Canada estimated one male at ~800 kg (1,700 lb). The often-repeated 1,002 kg Kotzebue Sound (Alaska, 1960) male is unverified (only forums/content sites).

wild_population.source_name: IUCN Red List assessment (Wiig et al. 2015): 19 subpopulations, ~26,000 (95% CI 22,000–31,000)

stronghold.evidence: Canada holds ~16,000 of ~26,000 polar bears (~two-thirds), 13 subpopulations

species.fun_fact: Polar bears have one of the lowest reproductive rates of any mammal.
species.notes: A newer IUCN assessment ID (22823/217912462) appears in search results (reported as assessed 2022, published 2025, still VU) but could not be opened; category VU either way. Range states include Greenland (Denmark) — native_continents lists North America/Europe(Svalbard)/Asia(Russia). Typical male figure is seasonal (spring vs autumn).

male_mass_kg.text: NPS Katmai: most adult males typically weigh 600–900 lb (272–408 kg) in mid-summer; by Oct–Nov large males can exceed 1,000 lb (454 kg).
male_mass_kg.source_name: NPS – Katmai Brown Bear FAQ

mass_cross_check.source_name: ADF&G Afognak/Sitkalidak report: mean male 209.4 kg (n=14, June captures)

max_mass_kg.text: Heaviest wild Kodiak reported at 751 kg (1,656 lb), reportedly shot 1894; found only on Wikipedia/secondary pages. Captive Kodiak 'Goliath' reportedly >900 kg (Guinness, captive).
max_mass_kg.source_name: Wikipedia – Kodiak bear (cross-check); Guinness World Records – heaviest carnivore on land

wild_population.source_name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance fact sheet citing McLellan et al. 2017 (IUCN)

stronghold.evidence: Russia >100,000 (SDZ/IUCN-based), roughly half the global total; Russian ministry claims ~308,000 (2026, unverified method). Next: US (Alaska), Canada

species.fun_fact: Brown bears may hibernate for up to seven months a year.
species.notes: Huge regional variation (>10%): coastal Alaska/Kodiak males 272–635 kg (USFWS Kodiak), interior grizzlies ~227 kg max (ADF&G), June Afognak mean 209 kg; European/Asian bears smaller. Chosen value (Katmai mid-summer) is coastal and biased high — consider a lower species-wide figure (~200–300 kg). Kodiak bear (U. a. middendorffi) is a subspecies, fold into fun fact. IUCN 2017 global LC; IUCN figure '110,000 mature individuals' appears for the global assessment in search summary vs 200,000+ total individuals.

male_mass_kg.text: Regional means of adult males: California 86 kg, Great Smoky Mtns 112 kg, Yellowstone 119 kg, north-central Minnesota 125 kg (compiled studies).
male_mass_kg.source_name: American black bear – compiled regional studies (Wikipedia mirror; cross-check only)

max_mass_kg.source_name: NC Wildlife Resources Commission – Black Bear

wild_population.source_name: IUCN Red List (Garshelis et al. 2016) working continental estimate, via secondary summary; Canada >380,000, US 339,000–465,000, Mexico 5,000–6,000

stronghold.evidence: Official 2016 estimates: Canada >380,000 vs United States 339,000–465,000 — ranges overlap, cannot rank reliably

species.fun_fact: American black bears outnumber all other bear species combined, about two to one.
species.notes: Typical male far below 250 kg — likely out of Top 30. Only Wikipedia-derived regional means found for typical mass (flag). IUCN page for U. americanus not seen; LC/2016/increasing from secondary summaries citing Garshelis et al. 2016. Stronghold US vs CA ambiguous (overlapping ranges).

male_mass_kg.text: San Diego Zoo fact sheet: males 100–261 kg in the wild (all subspecies); up to 325 kg in zoos. Amur males 180–306 kg.
male_mass_kg.source_name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance – Tiger fact sheet

max_mass_kg.text: Top of the wild range (Chitwan, Nepal, males 200–261 kg captured early 1970s); Smithsonian says Amur males up to 300 kg. Heavier claims are hunting records of doubtful reliability.
max_mass_kg.source_name: San Diego Zoo fact sheet / Smithsonian National Zoo

wild_population.source_name: IUCN Red List (Goodrich et al. 2022): 3,140 (2,608–3,905) mature individuals

stronghold.evidence: All-India Tiger Estimation 2022: average 3,682 tigers (3,167–3,925), ~75% of world's wild tigers

species.fun_fact: Tigers have lost more than 93% of their historic range in the past 100 years.
species.notes: Typical male (~180–235 kg depending on population: central India mean ~190 kg, Chitwan mean 235 kg) is below 250 kg — likely out of Top 30. IUCN trend: search summary said 'decreasing' but this could not be confirmed on the assessment page; left unknown — verify. India count (3,682 total incl. subadults) vs IUCN 3,140 mature are different units.

male_mass_kg.text: San Diego Zoo fact sheet: males 150–225 kg; average adult male lion 175 kg.
male_mass_kg.source_name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance – Lion fact sheet

max_mass_kg.text: Record male of 272 kg shot near Mt Kenya — widely repeated, no primary source seen; Kruger NP max recorded male 225 kg.

wild_population.source_name: IUCN Red List 2023 assessment: ~23,000 adult and subadult lions in Africa, ~670 in India

stronghold.evidence: TAWIRI 2024/25 national census ~17,200 lions vs South Africa 3,284, Botswana 3,064, Kenya 2,515

species.fun_fact: Wild Asiatic lions survive in just one place: India's Gir Forest region.
species.notes: Typical male below 250 kg — likely out of Top 30. Tanzania census (~17,200) is large relative to IUCN's ~23,000 Africa-wide (different methods/years) — flag. Max-mass record unverified (only forums/content sites).

male_mass_kg.text: Males 380–450 kg (avg 430 kg); school resource lists males 430 kg, females 386 kg.
male_mass_kg.source_name: animalinfo.org – Grevy's zebra

mass_cross_check.source_name: Grevy's Zebra school resource (PILAfrica): male 430 kg

wild_population.source_name: Great Grevy's Rally 2018 (northern Kenya census: 2,812, up from 2,350 in 2016)

stronghold.evidence: ~95% of world population in Kenya (Laikipia, Samburu); small isolated groups in southern Ethiopia

species.fun_fact: Grévy's zebra is the largest living wild member of the horse family.
species.notes: IUCN EN (Rubenstein et al. 2016) per San Diego Zoo fact sheet; IUCN page not seen; trend 'stable' from secondary only — verify. Population fell from ~13,700 (1977) to ~2,680 (2016). Grévy's Zebra Trust review gives 3,318 including 491 captive. Mass sources are secondary/educational; ADW page exists but data not read (WebFetch blocked).

male_mass_kg.text: San Diego Zoo fact sheet: male 220–373 kg.
male_mass_kg.source_name: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance – Plains zebra fact sheet

mass_cross_check.source_name: World Land Trust: 290–340 kg, males slightly larger

wild_population.source_name: IUCN 2016 (King & Moehlman): 150,000–250,000 mature; total >500,000 per World Land Trust

stronghold.evidence: 2016 official estimates table: Tanzania ~260,000, Botswana 99,500, Kenya 98,820; Kenya+Tanzania hold ~75% (SDZ citing King & Moehlman 2016)

species.fun_fact: The extinct quagga was not a separate species but a southern form of the plains zebra.
species.notes: Mass sources vary widely (African Conservation: males up to 320 kg; activewild 175–385 kg); typical male ~250–320 kg, borderline for Top 30. Country table from an aggregator (biodb) citing IUCN 2016 — verify against IUCN. Declining in 10 of 17 range states.

male_mass_kg.text: Animal Diversity Web: 250 to 440 kg (sexes combined); popular fact sheets give males 350–400 kg, females 250–300 kg.
male_mass_kg.source_name: Animal Diversity Web – Equus kiang

wild_population.source_name: CMS Central Asian Mammals Initiative – Equus kiang

stronghold.evidence: ~90% in China (Xizang 37,000–48,000; Qinghai/Gansu 15,000; Xinjiang 4,500–5,500); outside China 1,600–2,145

species.fun_fact: The kiang of the Tibetan Plateau is the largest wild ass in the world.
species.notes: Male-specific mass only from popular fact sheets (350–400 kg); ADW range is sex-combined. IUCN LC per Wikipedia/secondary (IUCN 3.1); assessment year 2015 and 'stable' trend not confirmed on IUCN page — verify. Taxonomy: sometimes treated as subspecies of E. hemionus; IUCN treats as species.

male_mass_kg.text: National Geographic: weight 440–750 lb (~200–340 kg), sexes not separated.
male_mass_kg.source_name: National Geographic – Przewalski's horse

wild_population.source_name: News reports 2024: ~1,000 wild-living in three Mongolian sites (Hustai ~423–450)

stronghold.evidence: ~1,000 free-ranging in Hustai, Khomiin Tal and Great Gobi B; smaller reintroductions in China, Kazakhstan, Russia

species.fun_fact: Every living Przewalski's horse descends from just 12 wild-caught founders.
species.notes: IUCN assesses the species Equus ferus (Przewalski's horse is the only wild population): EN, assessed 2014 by King, Boyd, Zimmermann & Kendall (published 2015, amended 2016), 178 mature wild individuals, trend increasing (per SDZ bibliography + Wikipedia list; IUCN page not seen). History: Extinct in the Wild 1960s–1996, then CR, downlisted to EN 2011. Mongolian national Red List: CR. Typical mass ~250–300 kg, sexes not separated — borderline; no stallion-specific figure found. Debate whether a true wild horse (feral-descended Botai link) — not checked.

male_mass_kg.text: Adults typically 250–320 kg, some up to 540 kg; females larger and heavier than males (Wikipedia; no sex-specific primary figure found).
male_mass_kg.source_name: Wikipedia – Malayan tapir (cross-check only; no better source found)

max_mass_kg.text: Wikipedia: some adults up to 540 kg — likely captive, unverified.

wild_population.source_name: IUCN (Traeholt et al. 2016) via ESABII / secondary

stronghold.evidence: Peninsular Malaysia ~1,500–2,000 (IUCN-based, ESABII) vs Sumatra <400–500 adults, Thailand/Myanmar <250; but 2026 Malaysian govt estimate only 700–800

species.fun_fact: It is the only tapir in the Old World and the largest of the world's tapirs.
species.notes: Females are the larger sex (10–20% heavier per a game wiki; Wikipedia 'larger and heavier'). Mass only from Wikipedia — needs a better source (e.g. ADW/IUCN TSG). Malaysian population figures conflict by >2x (1,300–2,000 older vs 700–800 2026 govt, Mongabay). IUCN e.T21472A45173636 (2016) per Wikipedia reference; page not seen.

species.fun_fact: Baird's tapir is the largest native land mammal of Central America.

species.fun_fact: Okapi females are bigger than males — rare among mammals.

species.notes: IUCN split Galápagos tortoises into ~12–13 species; no source definitively names the single largest species. Chose C. porteri (SF Zoo: 'one of the larger'); alternative C. vandenburghi (Volcán Alcedo, Isabela): up to ~320 kg, IUCN VU, ~6,320 individuals (largest population after Wolf Volcano C. becki ~7,000–8,000). IUCN CR (Cayot, Gibbs, Tapia & Caccone 2017) per Wikipedia/secondary; IUCN page not seen (ID 9026 per secondary). Trend 'increasing' per Wikipedia ('numbers rising'), unverified. Combined Galápagos total ~24,600–27,300 (IUCN-based secondary). Typical male ~300 kg qualifies for ≥250 kg.

Typical male ~250 kg — exactly at the threshold; maximum (PBS 305 kg) is a 'free-roaming' animal, location unclear.
